A `.ts` file with one NUL byte in a comment is valid JS but binary to git: a 2001-line `anthill-frontend/big.ts` gave `linesChanged: 0`, so checkSize passes far over the 400-line limit. `git diff --numstat --text` still prints `-` for it, so `--text` is not a fix. A `.gitattributes` with `* -diff` (not ring 0, not locked) merged once in a ring-2 directory does the same for every later change there.
cli.fix: For each binary record, compute lines yourself: count '\n' in the old and new blobs (`git cat-file blob <sha>`, using the shas from the --raw output) and add them, or charge max(lines, ceil(bytes/80)). Or fail the size gate whenever a binary file sits outside an explicit allowlist of binary extensions. Also add `**/.gitattributes` to the locked/ring-0 paths in the rules (a separate rules change).

cli.description: CI `gates` breaks its contract and can never pass in the shipped workflow. The README says: 'In CI its working tree is the base; the head is only fetched. Never check out or run anything from --head.' commons-gates.yml checks out `github.sha` (the base). gatesCi (~L621-630) refuses unless HEAD == --head and every expanded submodule is checked out at its new sha, so every PR exits 2, and every gitlink bump (where all kernel and UI code lives) exits 2 as well. It fails closed, but the authoritative gate is dead. The obvious operator 'fix' is to check out the PR head with `submissions: recursive` inside pull_request_target, using the PR's .gitmodules URLs and persisted credentials: the classic pwn-request setup.
cli.fix: Do not require the working tree at head. Materialise head into a temporary directory, as submissionGates does but without linking it to the repo: `git read-tree` into a private GIT_INDEX_FILE plus `checkout-index --prefix=<tmp>/`, with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1` and filters disabled. Do the same for each gitlink at its new sha, using objects fetched from the base's submodule remotes. Run checkRingImports against that directory. Keep the dirty or wrong-head check only as an opt-in `--worktree` mode.

cli.description: Commit names are not pinned to SHAs, which opens TOCTOU between gating and merging. The ledger accepts any non-empty string as baseCommit/headCommit. `submit --patch` and `submit --files` pass --base/--head through unvalidated. submissionGates resolves them for the diff, but then runs `git worktree add ... s.headCommit` with the raw string (~L664). A submission with headCommit `refs/remotes/origin/feature`, a short sha, `HEAD@{1}` or `:/some message` is gated on whatever it resolves to now. The bridge, a later human `commons merge`, and reviewers see whatever it resolves to later, and the ref can be moved between gate and merge.
cli.fix: In submissionGates, fail a gate (or raise a harness error) unless both commits match /^[0-9a-f]{40}$|^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ and resolveCommit returns exactly that string. Use the resolved sha for `worktree add` (after `--`). In `submit`, apply the same check to --base/--head for every source, not only --repo.

cli.description: --at is unbounded for local appends and also drives the evaluation clock. appendLocal passes --at straight to Ledger.append, which (unlike appendSigned) has no skew bound. ledger.ts itself warns that 'far-future freezes the ledger and expires every claim'. `settle --at 2099-...` vests every third-tranche merge and every clean-review settlement early, slashes every live claim as expired (settleExpiredClaims(nowIso)), and stamps the entries in 2099. After that the server can never accept another agent entry: it must be within 5 minutes of the clock and not before the head. `promote run --at <now+72h>` passes soakFloorHours and the recall window on time that has not passed, and appends a future-dated promotion.
cli.fix: For local appends, reject --at more than DEFAULT_MAX_SKEW_MS from io.now(), or use appendSigned with the clock bound. Keep any backdating or future-dating behind an explicit `--force-time` meant only for tests. For settle, promote check/run and metrics, use the wall clock (or the bounded stamp) as nowIso, never a free --at.

cli.description: Unexpanded gitlinks are not forced to ring 0. The README contract says: 'If expansion fails at any depth, report the bare gitlink path and classify it ring 0 whatever the rules say.' gitChanges records them in `unexpanded`, but staticGates and finishGates compute `submissionRing(change.files, rules)` from the globs alone. A nested gitlink added under `anthill-frontend/**` that cannot be fetched (attacker URL, missing commit) is reported as a ring-2 UI change, whose content nobody inspects.
cli.fix: In staticGates (both modes), set run.ring = 0 when change.unexpanded is non-empty and print why. In ledger mode, also fail declaredChange (or add an `expanded` gate) when unexpanded is non-empty, so the planner cannot merge an opaque pointer move.

cli.description: Attacker-controlled paths and details are printed raw. Git paths may contain newlines and control characters (the parser is correctly NUL-based). printChange, printReports and the coordinatorPass log write them unescaped to stdout. In the static CI job, a filename like `x\n::error::gates: PASS` or `\n::add-mask::...` injects GitHub workflow commands and fake 'PASS' lines into the log a human reads. In an operator's terminal, ESC/OSC sequences (title, OSC 52 clipboard write) from file names, finding ids or gate details get interpreted. The same strings are written into gateResult `details` with --record.
cli.fix: Escape any string that contains control characters before printing, for example print JSON.stringify(p) when /[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/ matches, the way core.quotePath does. Or refuse such paths with a failing gate (most reviewers would flag a filename containing a newline).

cli.description: submissionGates checks out the full untrusted head tree on the coordinator host before any size check, using the host's global git config. Blobs are deduplicated, so a tiny pack can expand into a huge checkout and fill the coordinator's disk; the ledger lives on that disk. A head with `.gitattributes`/`.lfsconfig` triggers a git-lfs smudge to an attacker URL if LFS is installed globally (SSRF). The coordinator repo's post-checkout hook also runs on attacker content.
cli.fix: Run gitChanges plus the size and declaredChange checks first, and skip the checkout (failing the gate) when the change exceeds rules.maxLinesPerSubmission or a file-count cap. Then materialise only what the ring gate needs, using read-tree plus checkout-index (or sparse checkout) into a plain directory with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c filter.lfs.process= -c filter.lfs.smudge= -c filter.lfs.required=false` and GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1.

cli.description: `plant commit --salt` accepts any operator-chosen salt. plantCommitment(submissionId, salt) is published before the plant is submitted. With a guessable salt (a word, a date, a short counter), any reviewer can test each new submission id against the open plantCommit entries and spot the plants: they catch them to avoid missedPlantPenalty and rubber-stamp everything else, which defeats the recall measurement.
cli.fix: Remove --salt, or require at least 32 random bytes in hex (/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/) and refuse anything else.

completedFixes.github:
I fixed 15 of the 17 issues in /home/user/anthill/anthill-commons/src/github.ts, added regression tests, and narrowed the remaining two (exact headCommit sha, issues 5 and 10) to a tree-and-parent binding. `node --import tsx --test test/github.test.ts` passes 51/51, none skipped. The real-git test ran, and the fake now hashes trees the way git does, so it matches `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`. tsc reports no errors in github.ts or its test. On the original code, the 200k-line edit throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` and the garbage-after-hunk patch is accepted; both are now refused with a PatchError.

The full suite gives 574/578. The 4 failures are signature/auth errors on upload (401/403) in server.test.ts tests 9–11 and client.test.ts "end to end". tsc also errors in playground.ts:154 and server.ts:801. Those modules are being edited concurrently and the failures are not patch-parsing related; the `summarisePatch` tests pass.

**Fixes by issue:**
1. **Base not in the branch (critical):** before any write, `GET compare/{baseCommit}...{tip}` must return `ahead`, otherwise PatchError. A test covers the "rejected commons branch" attack (`behind`) and unrelated history (`diverged`), with no writes.
2. **Same-repo push (high):**
   - `headRepo: {owner, repo}` is now required. Writes go to the fork, and the PR is opened with `head: "<bot>:commons/<id>"` and `maintainer_can_modify: false`.
   - Pushing into the project repo itself is refused unless `allowSameRepoHead: true`.
   - Paths under `.github/` (any case, rename sources included) are refused unless the caller passes an `allowDotGithub(path)` that returns true.
   - The file header says the bot token must not have `workflow` scope and that Actions should be off on the fork.
3. **Write cost (medium):**
   - `PATCH_LIMITS = {files: 300, lines: 100000}` is checked in parsePatch, so a refused patch costs no requests.
   - File contents go inline as `content` in `POST git/trees`, with no blob POSTs. Every patch costs four writes: tree, commit, ref, PR.
   - All base checks are reads that finish before the first write. A test puts the bad section last and asserts nothing was written.
4. **Stack overflow (medium):** applyHunks now appends in a loop. A test edits near the end of a 200k-line file.
5 and 10. **Linking to the signed headCommit:** partly rejected.
   - Reproducing the agent's exact sha is not possible in general: headCommit may be several commits with the agent's own identity and timestamps, and a squash merge makes a new commit anyway.
   - Instead, `expectedTree` is required, and the created tree must equal it before commit, ref or PR exist. The PR head is then "parent = s.baseCommit, tree = tree(s.headCommit)", which anyone with the repo can check.
   - `mergePullRequest` has an optional `expectedTree` guard as well.
6. **listChangedFiles (medium):** takes a required `expectedHeadSha`. It reads the PR before and after paging and requires the same head both times plus GitHub's `changed_files` count; a head mismatch throws 409.
7. **Lookalike paths (low):** checkRepoPath accepts printable ASCII only. It refuses `\`, `:` and `"`, segments ending in a dot or space, `.git`, `git~1`, `.gitmodules` and `gitmod~1`. Bidi and invisible characters are refused because they are not ASCII.
8. **Title and body (low):** the title must be one line of 1–256 characters with no control or bidi characters. I added `fenceUntrusted(text)` for participant text in PR bodies and comments; it fences the text so @mentions inside do not notify and the text cannot close the fence. The bridge does not fence bodies itself.
9 and 16. **Redirects:** every request uses `redirect: "manual"`, and any 3xx throws a GitHubError with its status. A test returns 307 to another host and checks only one request was made.
11. **Timeouts:** `timeoutMs` (default 30s) covers both the fetch and the body read. The fetch is aborted and the error is GitHubError(0, "timeout"). Tests cover a fetch that never resolves and a body that never arrives.
12. **Idempotent merge:**
   - New `findPullRequest(owner, repo, submissionId, headOwner)` prefers a merged PR, then an open one.
   - When the merge PUT gets 405, 409 or 422, mergePullRequest re-reads the PR and returns its merge commit if it was merged at the guarded sha.
13. **Retries:**
   - The bridge never deletes the branch now.
   - On a 422 from ref creation, it reuses the existing branch only if that commit has the same tree and parent; otherwise it throws 422 and leaves the branch alone.
   - On a 422 or lost reply from PR creation, it returns the existing open PR if its head and base match.
   - The old test that asserted the branch is deleted was replaced.
14. **Hunk structure (low):** parsePatch now checks header syntax, line tags, counts, order and offsets, and refuses trailing lines, so the server refuses malformed patches at upload.
15. **One-shot merge signature (low):** `mergePullRequest(owner, repo, n, sha, mergeOpts?, ghOpts?)` now matches the client method, including title and body.
17. **Base moved before merge (low):** optional `expectedBase` guard. A PR already merged is recognised before the guards run.

**API changes others must adopt:**
- `openPullRequest` needs `headRepo` and `expectedTree`, and returns `treeSha`.
- `listChangedFiles` takes a 4th argument, `expectedHeadSha`.
- `mergePullRequest`'s 5th argument is now a `MergeOptions` object: `{title, body, expectedTree, expectedBase}`.
- New exports: `findPullRequest`, `fenceUntrusted`, `PATCH_LIMITS`, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PullRequestInfo`, `MergeOptions`, `RepoRef`.
- `FetchLike`'s init now always carries `redirect` and `signal`; global fetch satisfies it.

**Remaining issues:**
- The PR head commit sha is GitHub's and is not in the ledger. It is bound only by tree and parent.
- A dangling tree object is written when the expected tree does not match. That costs one write and is harmless.
- `expectedBase` checks the base branch tip just before the PUT, so a direct push to dev in between could still slip through.
- Not checked against live GitHub: that a fork-network base commit and base tree resolve when used as `parents` and `base_tree` in the fork, and that `head_repo` is accepted for a same-owner fork.

**Changes needed in modules owned by others:**
- **Bridge wiring (cli.ts or integrator), `GithubBridge.merge(s)` in coordinator.ts:** call `findPullRequest(owner, repo, s.id, botForkOwner)`, then `mergePullRequest(owner, repo, pr.number, pr.headSha, { expectedTree: <git rev-parse s.headCommit^{tree}>, expectedBase? })`, and record the returned sha. This makes the merge idempotent, which coordinator.ts:398 requires. The merge runs under the ledger lock and can make up to five requests, so pass a `timeoutMs` that fits the lock budget.
- **server.ts `onPatch` handler (wired in cli.ts):** call `openPullRequest` with `headRepo` set to the bot fork, `baseCommit: s.baseCommit`, and `expectedTree` from the coordinator clone. The clone must already have the objects for `s.headCommit`; if it does not, defer and retry. The title must be one line, and participant text goes through `fenceUntrusted`. Pass `allowDotGithub` only after airlock approval.
- **Ring and airlock checks on a live PR:** use `listChangedFiles(..., pr.headSha)`, not `OpenedPullRequest.files`.
- **cli.ts `isCanonicalPath`:** align with `checkRepoPath` (printable ASCII, no `:`, no trailing dot or space, no `.gitmodules`), so `submit --files` cannot sign a submission whose paths the bridge will later refuse.
- **ARCHITECTURE.md:** has no `src/github.ts` section. Someone who owns it should add the contract above.

The duplicate reports (findings blocking merges: #3/#12; promotion re-check: #8/#13; upload signatures: #10/#23) are fixed once each.

## What changed

**Patch binding (critical #2).** Every submission is now first bound to its uploaded patch, before gates.
- A new `bindPatch` action calls an injected `ExecuteDeps.bindPatch(s)`. It returns `{head, patchSha256}`, `null` (no patch yet) or `{error}` (the patch does not apply).
- The result is recorded as a coordinator `gateResult` with gate `"patch"` and details `canonical({head, patchSha256})`. This uses an existing entry kind, so `types.ts` is untouched. The gate name is reserved: a gate runner cannot report it.
- Gates, finding reproduction and the merge all use the bound head, never the author's declared `headCommit`.
- `GithubBridge.merge(submission, expectedHead)` now receives the bound head, for the bridge to pass as its sha guard.
- `headBinding: "declared"` trusts the declared head and is meant only for an operator's own repository. The default is `"required"`, and with no binder configured the action fails loudly.

**Sandbox (critical #1), partly fixed.** `localReproducer` now refuses to run without a `sandbox` argv. It forwards `sandbox`, `timeoutMs` and `env`. The refusal is thrown rather than reported as a harness error, so a misconfigured coordinator never voids findings. The header documents that the sandbox must be a separate uid or container. Moving gates and the bridge out of the process is deployment work.

**Findings that block forever (#3, #12).**
- `voidFinding` closes a finding as not reproduced, with logDigest `void:no-test` or `void:harness-error`. That happens when no test is uploaded within `findingGraceHours` (default 24), or after `maxHarnessErrors` (default 3).
- The executor counts harness errors in `ExecuteDeps.harnessErrors`. This count is in memory, so a restart resets it.
- At most `maxReproductionsPerPass` (default 4) reproductions are planned per pass, oldest first. They run concurrently, two at a time by default, beside the rest of the pass; snapshot and promote wait for them.
- On the server, submission and finding ids must be safe file names, and every stake must be covered by `availableReputation`.

**Review quorum (#5).** A merge needs a quorum of revealed assigned reviews: `reviewQuorum`, default max(1, assigned − 1). If the window closes below quorum, the submission never merges.

**Phase-1 finding confirmation (#6).** In phase 1, a reproduced finding pays, slashes and records an escape only after `findingConfirmed`. It blocks the merge regardless.

**Re-checks under the lock (#8, #13).**
- Merge re-runs the whole `mergeReadiness`, with a freshly asked human approval, through the new required `ExecuteDeps.recheck`. `runOnce` builds it, so `RunDeps` is unchanged for callers.
- Promote re-runs `ancestryProblems` and `evaluatePromotion`, then fast-forwards main, all under the lock.
- Snapshot re-checks its submissions under the lock.

**Snapshots and plants (#14).** A snapshot covers only the clean prefix of merges in merge order. Dev is linear, so a defective submission blocks every snapshot after it until reverted, and a pending finding makes it wait. While a plant commitment is unrevealed, merges of later submissions wait for the window to close plus `plantRevealGraceHours` (default 1).

**Smaller planner fixes.**
- The review window fails closed when `entries` is missing (#16).
- A suspended author's submissions are skipped (#20).
- The external entropy is recorded in the assignment log line (#22).
- `RunDeps.patchesDir` defaults `patchAvailable` and `findingTestAvailable` from the uploads on disk (#21).
- `approvedTasks` and `honeytokenHits` turn into `task` and `honeytoken` actions (#15).

**Server rate limits and flooding (#4, #7).**
- Signatures are verified outside the lock.
- A token is charged only after the head check, the at-check and the revocation check pass. Replayed entries (409) and revoked keys (403 `signer-revoked`) cost the owner nothing.
- New limits: a per-IP bucket before anything is read, a cap on concurrent requests (503), and a cap on the lock queue (503, using the new `LedgerStore.depth()`).
- A 413 drops the connection once answered.
- An upload's author key is checked before its body is read.

**Server size caps (#9).** Default `entryBytes` is now 32 KiB. `FIELD_CAPS` limits every string, array and named field, and there is a per-owner daily byte quota.

**Admin ingress (#15).** `ownerKey`, `plantCommit`, `plantReveal` and `rulesChange` are accepted on `/api/entries` when signed by a genesis admin key.

**Upload signatures (#10, #23).** Uploads are now signed over `uploadMessage(route, id, sha256)` = `canonical({purpose:"commons-upload/v1", route, id, sha256})`. Bare-digest signatures are accepted only with `acceptLegacyUploadSignatures`. `client.ts` already uses `uploadMessage`.

**Assignments (#11, #19).**
- Author-written fields are returned under `untrusted`, and patch responses carry `X-Commons-Untrusted`.
- An assignment is no longer listed once its commits are closed (a verdict revealed, a plant revealed, a finding reproduced) or when the agent is revoked.

**Test fixes (#17, #18).**
- The rate-limit test refills exactly one token, sends 5 forged posts, then checks the genuine post succeeds and the next one is refused.
- The fake claim stake is now 40, above the ledger's floor of 15.
- There is a new test for the fallback handler.

Every issue has a regression test.

## Changes needed in others' modules
- **`cli.ts` `coordinatorPass`:**
  - Pass `bindPatch` from the bridge. Alternatively pass `plan.headBinding: "declared"`, but only behind an explicit flag for a trusted local repository.
  - Pass `sandbox` and `timeoutMs` to `localReproducer`.
  - Pass `patchesDir: dir`.
  - Pass a `harnessErrors` Map that lives across passes in the `serve` loop.
  - The `commons settle` command, which calls `planActions` in phase 1, now holds reproduced-finding settlements until `findingConfirmed`. It needs a confirm option or phase 2.
- **`github.ts` / bridge:**
  - Implement `bindPatch(s)`: build the bot commit from `baseCommit` plus the stored patch, open or update the bot PR, and return `{head, patchSha256 = sha256hex(stored file)}`.
  - `merge(s, expectedHead)` must pass `expectedHead` as `mergePullRequest`'s sha and refuse if the PR head moved.
- **`client.ts`:**
  - The `Assignment` type is stale: `taskId`, `baseCommit`, `headCommit`, `changedFiles` and `linesChanged` now sit under `untrusted`.
  - The reviewer role prompt must treat `untrusted` and the patch as data.
  - Fix the fake server in `test/client.test.ts` to verify `uploadMessage`.
- **`ledger.ts`:**
  - Accept a superseding `reviewAssignment` after the window closes below quorum, and reopen commits for the newly drawn reviewers. Today it rejects with `assigned`, and commits close on the first reveal. Without this, a submission below quorum stalls for good.
  - Optionally, reload the file when it grows by valid lines instead of going `stale`.
- **`types.ts` + `incentives.ts`:**
  - A `SettlementReason` and settle function for reviewers who committed and never revealed. `revealPhaseClose` still only calls a callback.
  - An `entropy` field on `reviewAssignment`, so `verifyAssignment` can recompute the beacon from the ledger alone.
  - A `testSha256` field on `finding`, so the test cannot be chosen after filing.
  - A dedicated patch-binding entry kind would be cleaner than the `"patch"` gateResult.
- **`findings.ts`:** a head-only timeout counts as a harness error. After 3 such errors the finding is now voided and the finder slashed, even if the head's code genuinely hangs. Worth reconsidering.

## Remaining issues
- **Deployment (#1):** the GitHub bridge needs its own process so the token is out of the loop's environment. The coordinator key must be readable only by the ledger writer. Gate runners that execute submission code, such as `behaviourDelta`, must run sandboxed.
- **Reverts:** a defective merged submission blocks later snapshots, and no action exists yet to revert it.
- **Findings (#6):** the author-dispute flow, and running findings against acceptance specs or hidden mutations, are not built.
- **Honeytoken (#11):** no honeytoken is placed in reviewer assignments.
- **Per-IP limit:** it keys on the socket address. Behind a reverse proxy every client shares one bucket, and I deliberately do not trust `X-Forwarded-For`.

## Agent-kit review fixes: all 22 issues checked, every real one fixed

`test/client.test.ts` now has **38 tests, all passing, none skipped**. That includes the sandbox test, which ran here as root using the `nobody` user. Type checking (`tsc --noEmit`) shows no errors in my files.

The full `npm test` run is **670 pass, 2 fail**. Both failures are in `test/cli.test.ts` and neither touches my files:
- `commons init --at ... is more than 5 minutes from the clock`
- `no patch binder configured (ExecuteDeps.bindPatch)`

There are also type errors in other people's files: `src/cli.ts:1814`, `src/playground.ts:154` and `test/incentives.test.ts`.

**One regression was already live before this change.** `server.ts` had moved to signing uploads with `uploadMessage(...)`, but the client still signed the bare digest. Every real patch and finding-test upload was getting 401, and the end-to-end test was failing. It is fixed now.

## What changed, by issue

**1 and 12: `headCommit`.**
- `coordinator.ts` already gates, reproduces and merges against the commit bound to the uploaded patch, so the exploit itself is closed on the server side.
- On my side, I added `commonsCommit({repoDir, baseCommit, patch, submissionId})`. It applies the patch to the base in a temporary index and commits with a fixed identity, date and message, so anyone holding the base gets the same sha. These are exported as `COMMONS_COMMIT_IDENTITY` and `commonsCommitMessage`. It writes the git objects and runs from the repo's top level.
- `submit()` with `repoDir` now declares that sha, resolves `--base` to a full sha, and refuses a `--head` that differs.
- New `commons-agent head-commit` command, so reviewers can check the declared head. `worker.md` and the README no longer say to send your local sha.

**2: strangers' code ran in the reviewer's VM.**
- New `agent-kit/bin/run-untrusted`. It runs a throwaway copy as a separate user, with `env -i`, `unshare --net`, no access to `~/.commons`, a timeout, and kills that user's processes afterwards.
- Every role now runs repo code only through it, uses `mktemp -d` for scratch files, and commits only after all sandboxed runs finish.

**3: kit loaded from the checkout under review.** README §1 now installs the kit from a pinned commit (`git archive` + `npm ci --ignore-scripts`) into `/opt/commons-kit`, outside the checkout. Prompts use absolute paths. Owner-key commands are documented as running only from such an install.

**4: leaked agent key.**
- The README's description of what a leaked key can do is corrected.
- The client now refuses stakes above `maxStake` (default 320, set with `COMMONS_MAX_STAKE`) before posting.
- One part rejected: moving the key from the environment variable to a file. The variable is the only way a secret reaches a cloud VM. The protection is that strangers' code runs as another user with no environment and no network, so it can't read the variable or send anything out.

**5: commands copied from content.** Roles now say: build every command from the base commit's CI config or a fixed template with a checked path. Never run `Evidence.command` or `finding.testCommand` verbatim.

**6: honeytoken quoting.** Roles now say to describe an injected instruction in your own words with file and line, and never reproduce its wording, URLs or tokens.

**7, 8, 15, 19: Unicode in `openrouter-review.ts`.**
- Hidden characters are now replaced with visible markers like `⟦U+200D⟧` instead of being deleted, so identifiers that differ only by a joiner stay distinct.
- Hidden tag-character text is decoded and shown as `⟦hidden: "..."⟧`.
- U+2028/2029 become a new line that keeps the diff prefix, and are counted and reported.
- The character set now uses `\p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}`, and the header comment is corrected.

**9: model and data policy.**
- The first-pass reconstruction is labelled as untrusted and capped, and the model is told to re-check it against the diff.
- Router ids like `openrouter/auto` are refused, and a response from a different model than requested is rejected.
- Requests set `data_collection: "deny"`.

**10: uploads and resubmission.**
- Uploads now sign `uploadMessage(route, id, sha)`; there is a test that a captured signature can't be replayed to another submission.
- The submission id is printed before posting. A failed upload throws `SubmissionUploadError` naming the id, and there is a new `upload-patch` command so nobody resubmits.

**11: CLI key handling.** `register-agent` and `revoke-agent` require `--owner-key-file` and refuse while `COMMONS_AGENT_KEY` is set. Every command prints the signing keyId to stderr. `keygen` refuses a path inside a git working tree unless `--force` is given.

**13: spec delivery.** `spec-writer.md` now delivers via the channel the coordinator names, falling back to the taskless submission in protocol.md §5.2 (with a warning that its test gate will fail), and never with `--task <taskId>`.

**14: claim dates.** `claim()` now accepts any date `Date.parse` reads and sends the `toISOString()` form; it refuses unparseable input.

**16: event trigger.** The README now says to use a schedule for reviewers, not the PR-opened event, and explains why.

**17: reveal lock-out.** `reviewer.md` and `attester.md` now say to commit early and reveal as the last step, with the lock-out risk stated plainly.

**18: ambiguous commit.** The salt record now stores the stake. A retry reuses it without calling `assignments()`, and `duplicate-commit` is turned into a "reveal it" message.

**20: alias and credits.** Shipped `agent-kit/bin/commons-agent` and `bin/openrouter-review` wrappers. They also move tsx's compile cache out of the shared `/tmp`, because another local user could plant files there. The credit sentence now mentions the free first submission.

**21: duplicated verdict code.** The client now uses `review.ts` `commitmentFor` and `validateVerdict`. `commitmentOf` and `verdictProblems` stay as re-exports only because `cli.ts` imports them.

**22: tests.**
- The race test now asserts that a 409 actually happened.
- Added tests for claim, `fileFinding` with a signed upload, and a 503 keeping the salt record.
- The end-to-end test now covers review assignment, commit and reveal, and a real 409, against the real `server.ts`.
- The fake server's assignments response matches the server's new nested `untrusted` shape.

## Remaining issues
- I couldn't check that GitHub's create-commit API, given the fixed identity, produces the same sha as `commonsCommit`.
- Reviewers can still lock each other out by revealing first; the role text only reduces the risk.
- The new marker characters `⟦ ⟧` aren't escaped, so a diff that contains them literally can imitate a marker.
- `run-untrusted` gives a separate user and no network, but it is not a VM. It needs root and Node installed somewhere other users can read.
